newsitem.title: UK: Stocks drop in Tokyo, edge lower in London.
newsitem.headline: Stocks drop in Tokyo, edge lower in London.

text.p: Here is how major stock markets outside the United States ended Monday.

LONDON - Shares retreated from Friday's record close as Wall Street also fell from last week's peaks, with markets cautious ahead of Tuesday's Senate testimony by Federal Reserve chief Alan Greenspan. The FTSE 100 index closed 13.7 points lower at 4,194.0 with decliners in a near two-to-one majority.

FRANKFURT - German shares, fuelled by the dollar, kept up their advance to record levels in bourse dealings but traders said they were wary about maintaining the gains for the near term. The 30-share DAX index ended bourse trade up 29.31 points at 3,030.68 points, a record.

PARIS - French stocks closed lower after the market tracked an early decline on Wall Street due to profit-taking. The blue-chip CAC-40 index finished down 19.0 points, or 0.78 percent, at 2,406.10 after giving up an early advance that lifted it an all-time intraday high of 2,438.50 earlier.

ZURICH - Swiss shares lost steam in the course of the day, giving up most initial gains and slipping below Friday's close towards the session's end. The SMI slid 10.3 points, or 0.26 percent, to 4,009.6. The All-share SPI fell 4.49 points to 2,574.67.

TOKYO - Japanese stocks took another steep tumble as the government failed to offer new economic initiatives in a closely watched policy speech and reaffirmed its resolve to raise taxes. The market's key barometer, the Nikkei 225 average, closed down 609.70 points, or 3.37 percent, at 17,480.34.

HONG KONG - Hong Kong's Hang Seng Index edged to its fourth straight record close, led by conglomerates, but ended off the day's highs as other stocks suffered profit-taking and Japanese shares fell. The Hang Seng rose 11.84 points, or 0.09 percent, to 13,868.24 after hitting a session high of 13,994.86.

SYDNEY - Another strong session from Wall Street, combined with hopes of a further local interest rate cut, boosted the Australian share market to a record close. The benchmark All Ordinaries index finished 8.7 points firmer at 2,444.2.

JOHANNESBURG - South African shares ended weaker after a morning surge ran out of steam at noon amid profit-taking and a weak gold price. Weaker London and Tokyo stocks also contributed to the weakness in local shares. The overall index lost 5.5 points to 6,777.4, the industrial index fell 2.6 points to 8,177.8 and the gold index lost 7.1. points to 1,419.1.
